title: Correlation Identifier

validation.research: Six primary sources: Hohpe and Woolf’s Correlation Identifier and Return Address catalogs; Hohpe’s Correlation and Conversations essay; RabbitMQ RPC tutorial; W3C Trace Context; and Stripe idempotent-request documentation. The article explains the originating request-ID form and broader Conversation Identifier alias, and separates envelope, business, trace, conversation, and idempotency identities. The inference that a whole-checkout trace ID can be too broad for several pending quote contexts is presented through an original example, not as a W3C application-matching guarantee.

example_limits: Original sequential shipping-quote matching simulation. Two conversations for O42 carry independent correlation IDs and recover distinct economy/express contexts. Envelope IDs can change across a simulated relay and each reply has its own message ID. A matcher owns up to two pending provider/order/mode contexts. Validated replies from the expected source consume one context; unknown, unexpected-source, duplicate, and abandoned answers do not consume other contexts. Forget models explicit owner disposal without a timer. Tokens are exact nonblank strings up to 128 characters; prices are nonnegative integer US dollar cents. Source identity is assumed to come from a trusted adapter; a caller-controlled string provides no authentication. Session freshness is an assumption, not a production unique-ID scheme. No broker, inbox routing, network, actual shipping computation, persistence, retry, server deduplication, automatic expiration, thread synchronization, remote cancellation, or restart recovery.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, commit, push, or pull request.
